1How to use this checklist

Every component has five levels. A component is mastered when all five are passed without notes, and someone else has seen it (sign the checkpoint). When every checkpoint and the final one are signed, you can stand behind the code.

1 · ExplainSay what it does and why, in your own words.
2 · InspectSee its live state with a command and read it correctly.
3 · BreakKill it and predict the result before you do.
4 · ReadWalk through its code and config line by line.
5 · ChangeMake a small change, deploy, prove it, revert.
Before every Break step: untick Auto-heal on the dashboard (otherwise it restarts your victim after 15 s). Run commands in Ubuntu from /mnt/d/HA_Trading_Lab. Everything stays inside the lab: the exchange is simulated, nothing touches IBKR or real money. Every inspect command in this list was tested on the running lab. After a Break step, bring everything back with Restore everything on the dashboard or docker compose up -d.

2Checkpoint 0: own the lab

  • git init && git add -A && git commit -m "baseline": every experiment can be undone with git checkout .
  • Start / stop / status: docker compose up -d · docker compose down · docker compose ps (38 running)
  • Logs: docker compose logs -f router-1 · docker logs --since 5m hal-control
  • Deploy one service: docker compose up -d --build --no-deps control
  • Read How Every Part Works once, end to end

4Final checkpoint: you can guarantee it

Pass all seven, without notes, in front of a reviewer.

  • Trace one real order end to end: its rows in orders, outbox, fills and notifications, its Kafka message and its exchange fill; explain every timestamp (guide, section 4).
  • Run every drill in the guide's test catalogue (section 7.4): write the prediction first, then compare. All audits 0.
  • Take a whole zone down and back up; explain every line of the event timeline.
  • Rebuild from nothing: docker compose down -v, start again, reach "audit all 0". Warning: -v deletes every volume, including the database and the backups: do it last, after the restore drill.
  • Restore drill: restore from a backup; state the RPO and RTO you measured.
  • Explain the limits: what the lab does not prove yet (real latency, network cuts, disk loss, 10× load).
  • Teach it: walk someone through How Every Part Works and demo a database failover live.
